title.en: Walking up the fell, I saw a raven
title.sl: Deležniški stavki: walking up, built in 1800
title.it: Le frasi participiali: walking up, built in 1800

goal.sl: Skrajšaš stavek z -ing, deležnikom in having (Walking up the fell, I saw a raven; a mill built in 1800), z istim osebkom za obe polovici.
goal.de: Du kürzt Sätze mit -ing, dem Partizip und having (Walking up the fell, I saw a raven; a mill built in 1800), mit demselben Subjekt für beide Hälften.
goal.it: Accorci le frasi con -ing, il participio e having (Walking up the fell, I saw a raven; a mill built in 1800), con lo stesso soggetto per le due metà.
goal.en: You can make a sentence shorter with -ing, the participle and having (Walking up the fell, I saw a raven; a mill built in 1800), with one subject for both halves.

say.sl: Dva stavka z istim osebkom skrajšaš z **-ing**: **Walking up the fell, I saw a raven.** (Ko sem se {m:vzpenjal|f:vzpenjala} na hrib, sem {m:videl|f:videla} krokarja.) To je isto kot **While I was walking up the fell, I saw a raven.** Osebek in was odpadeta. **Feeling cold, Jack shut the door.** (Ker ga je zeblo, je Jack zaprl vrata.) To se bolj piše kot govori.
say.de: Zwei Sätze mit demselben Subjekt kürzt du mit **-ing**: **Walking up the fell, I saw a raven.** (Als ich den Fell hinaufging, sah ich einen Raben.) Das ist dasselbe wie **While I was walking up the fell, I saw a raven.** Subjekt und was fallen weg. **Feeling cold, Jack shut the door.** (Weil ihm kalt war, machte Jack die Tür zu.) Das schreibt man öfter, als man es sagt.
say.it: Due frasi con lo stesso soggetto si accorciano con **-ing**, come col gerundio: **Walking up the fell, I saw a raven.** (Salendo sul fell, ho visto un corvo.) È come **While I was walking up the fell, I saw a raven.** Soggetto e was cadono. **Feeling cold, Jack shut the door.** (Sentendo freddo, Jack chiuse la porta.) Si scrive più di quanto si dica.
say.en: Two clauses with one subject get shorter with **-ing**: **Walking up the fell, I saw a raven.** That's the same as **While I was walking up the fell, I saw a raven.** The subject and was go. **Feeling cold, Jack shut the door.** You'll see this more in writing than in talk.

say.sl: Z **-ing** poveš tudi razlog, **not** gre naprej: **Not knowing the way, we asked at the inn.** (Ker nismo poznali poti, smo vprašali v gostilni.) **Being late, Sam ran to the bus.** Da bo jasneje, lahko pred -ing stoji mala beseda: **After eating, we went home.** **While waiting for the bus, I read the paper.** Po after, before in while tukaj -ing.
say.de: Mit **-ing** sagst du auch einen Grund, **not** kommt nach vorn: **Not knowing the way, we asked at the inn.** (Weil wir den Weg nicht kannten, fragten wir im Gasthaus.) **Being late, Sam ran to the bus.** Klarer wird es mit einem kleinen Wort davor: **After eating, we went home.** **While waiting for the bus, I read the paper.** Nach after, before und while hier -ing.
say.it: Con **-ing** dici anche un motivo, **not** va davanti: **Not knowing the way, we asked at the inn.** (Non conoscendo la strada, abbiamo chiesto alla locanda.) **Being late, Sam ran to the bus.** Per maggiore chiarezza, davanti può stare una parolina: **After eating, we went home.** **While waiting for the bus, I read the paper.** Dopo after, before e while qui -ing.
say.en: **-ing** gives a reason too, with **not** first: **Not knowing the way, we asked at the inn.** **Being late, Sam ran to the bus.** To be clearer, a small word can come before it: **After eating, we went home.** **While waiting for the bus, I read the paper.** After after, before and while here: -ing.

say.sl: Za samostalnikom **-ing** nadomesti who ali which z glagolom: **The man standing by the gate is Jack.** (Moški, ki stoji pri vratih, je Jack.) To je **The man who is standing by the gate**. **People living in the valley know him.** Na severu rečejo tudi *the man stood by the gate*; pisno je **standing**.
say.de: Nach einem Nomen ersetzt **-ing** who oder which mit dem Verb: **The man standing by the gate is Jack.** (Der Mann, der beim Tor steht, ist Jack.) Das ist **The man who is standing by the gate**. **People living in the valley know him.** Im Norden sagt man auch *the man stood by the gate*; geschrieben steht **standing**.
say.it: Dopo un nome **-ing** sostituisce who o which col verbo: **The man standing by the gate is Jack.** (L'uomo in piedi vicino al cancello è Jack.) È **The man who is standing by the gate**. **People living in the valley know him.** Al nord si dice anche *the man stood by the gate*; per iscritto si usa **standing**.
say.en: After a noun **-ing** takes the place of who or which and the verb: **The man standing by the gate is Jack.** That's **The man who is standing by the gate**. **People living in the valley know him.** In the North people also say *the man stood by the gate*; writing wants **standing**.

say.sl: Deležnik pomeni, da je bilo narejeno, namesto which was: **a mill built in 1800** (mlin, zgrajen leta 1800). **The cheese made on Jack's farm is the best.** Lahko stoji tudi na začetku: **Built in 1800, the mill is still there.** **Seen from the tarn, the fell looks small.** (Gledan z jezerca, je hrib videti majhen.) Nepravilne oblike ostanejo: built, made, written, seen.
say.de: Das Partizip heißt: Es wurde gemacht, statt which was: **a mill built in 1800** (eine 1800 gebaute Mühle). **The cheese made on Jack's farm is the best.** Es kann auch am Anfang stehen: **Built in 1800, the mill is still there.** **Seen from the tarn, the fell looks small.** (Vom Bergsee aus gesehen wirkt der Fell klein.) Die unregelmäßigen Formen bleiben: built, made, written, seen.
say.it: Il participio dice che è stato fatto, invece di which was: **a mill built in 1800** (un mulino costruito nel 1800). **The cheese made on Jack's farm is the best.** Può stare anche all'inizio: **Built in 1800, the mill is still there.** **Seen from the tarn, the fell looks small.** (Visto dal laghetto, il fell sembra piccolo.) Le forme irregolari restano: built, made, written, seen.
say.en: The participle says it was done, in place of which was: **a mill built in 1800**. **The cheese made on Jack's farm is the best.** It can come first too: **Built in 1800, the mill is still there.** **Seen from the tarn, the fell looks small.** The verbs keep their own forms: built, made, written, seen.

say.sl: **Having** + deležnik pove, da je bilo eno že končano, ko se je začelo drugo: **Having finished the hay, we went to the inn.** (Ko smo pospravili seno, smo šli v gostilno.) To je **After we had finished**. **Having lost the map, we turned back.** V govoru je pogostejše **After finishing the hay**.
say.de: **Having** + Partizip sagt, dass das eine schon vorbei war, als das andere begann: **Having finished the hay, we went to the inn.** (Nachdem wir mit dem Heu fertig waren, gingen wir ins Gasthaus.) Das ist **After we had finished**. **Having lost the map, we turned back.** Gesprochen ist **After finishing the hay** häufiger.
say.it: **Having** + participio dice che una cosa era già finita quando è cominciata l'altra: **Having finished the hay, we went to the inn.** (Finito di fare il fieno, siamo andati alla locanda.) È **After we had finished**. **Having lost the map, we turned back.** A voce è più comune **After finishing the hay**.
say.en: **Having** + the participle says one thing was over when the other began: **Having finished the hay, we went to the inn.** That's **After we had finished**. **Having lost the map, we turned back.** In talk **After finishing the hay** is more usual.

say.sl: Obe polovici imata isti osebek: **Walking up the fell, I saw a raven.** {m:Hodil|f:Hodila} sem jaz in {m:videl|f:videla} sem jaz. V *Walking up the fell, a raven flew over me* hodi po stavku krokar. Ljudje to rečejo in se razume, v skrbnem pisanju pa je **As I was walking up the fell, a raven flew over me.** Osebek takoj za vejico je tisti, ki hodi.
say.de: Beide Hälften haben dasselbe Subjekt: **Walking up the fell, I saw a raven.** Ich ging und ich sah. In *Walking up the fell, a raven flew over me* geht laut Satz der Rabe. Man sagt das und versteht es, aber sorgfältig geschrieben steht **As I was walking up the fell, a raven flew over me.** Das Subjekt gleich nach dem Komma ist der, der geht.
say.it: Le due metà hanno lo stesso soggetto: **Walking up the fell, I saw a raven.** Salivo io e ho visto io. In *Walking up the fell, a raven flew over me*, a stare alla frase, cammina il corvo. Si dice e si capisce, ma nello scritto curato si usa **As I was walking up the fell, a raven flew over me.** Il soggetto subito dopo la virgola è chi cammina.
say.en: Both halves have one subject: **Walking up the fell, I saw a raven.** I walked and I saw. In *Walking up the fell, a raven flew over me* the sentence has the raven walking. People say it and you understand them, but careful writing wants **As I was walking up the fell, a raven flew over me.** The subject right after the comma is the one walking.

exercises.text: ___ (walk) up the fell last week, Jack heard a lamb. ___ (leave) by its mother, it was very cold. ___ (not know) what to do, he carried it home. The sheep ___ (keep) on the fell are Herdwicks. The woman ___ (feed) the lamb now is his aunt. ___ (warm) by the fire, it soon got up.

accept: Walking
Left
Not knowing
kept
feeding
Warmed

translation.sl: Ko se je Jack prejšnji teden vzpenjal na hrib, je zaslišal jagnje. Mati ga je zapustila in zelo ga je zeblo. Ker ni vedel, kaj naj stori, ga je odnesel domov. Ovce, ki jih redijo na hribu, so pasme herdwick. Ženska, ki zdaj hrani jagnje, je njegova teta. Ogreto ob ognju, je kmalu vstalo.
translation.de: Als Jack letzte Woche den Fell hinaufging, hörte er ein Lamm. Von der Mutter verlassen, fror es sehr. Weil er nicht wusste, was er tun sollte, trug er es heim. Die Schafe auf dem Fell sind Herdwicks. Die Frau, die das Lamm jetzt füttert, ist seine Tante. Am Feuer aufgewärmt, stand es bald auf.
translation.it: Salendo sul fell la settimana scorsa, Jack ha sentito un agnello. Lasciato dalla madre, aveva molto freddo. Non sapendo che cosa fare, l'ha portato a casa. Le pecore tenute sul fell sono Herdwick. La donna che ora dà da mangiare all'agnello è sua zia. Scaldato vicino al fuoco, si è presto alzato.
translation.en: Walking up the fell last week, Jack heard a lamb. Left by its mother, it was very cold. Not knowing what to do, he carried it home. The sheep kept on the fell are Herdwicks. The woman feeding the lamb now is his aunt. Warmed by the fire, it soon got up.

translation.sl: Ko je zaslišala dež, je gospa Birkett zaprla okna. Moški, ki sedi ob ognju, je Stari Wilf. Packhorse, zgrajen leta 1750, ima debele zidove. Ker se nismo hoteli zmočiti, smo ostali notri. Ko je pojedel juho, je Wilf zaspal.
translation.de: Als sie den Regen hörte, schloss Mrs Birkett die Fenster. Der Mann beim Feuer ist der alte Wilf. Das 1750 gebaute Packhorse hat dicke Mauern. Weil wir nicht nass werden wollten, blieben wir drinnen. Nachdem er seine Suppe gegessen hatte, schlief Wilf ein.
translation.it: Sentendo la pioggia, Mrs Birkett ha chiuso le finestre. L'uomo seduto vicino al fuoco è il vecchio Wilf. Il Packhorse, costruito nel 1750, ha muri spessi. Non volendo bagnarci, siamo rimasti dentro. Finita la zuppa, Wilf si è addormentato.
translation.en: Hearing the rain, Mrs Birkett shut the windows. The man sitting by the fire is Old Wilf. The Packhorse, built in 1750, has thick walls. Not wanting to get wet, we stayed inside. Having finished his soup, Wilf fell asleep.
